intro: This repo has no build step and no CI. The steps below run the DAGs in the official Airflow Docker image. Most DAGs and most tests read the Greenstand databases. For access, ask in the automations-working-group Slack channel, as the README says.
prerequisites: Docker. The Airflow image includes Python 3.12 and the Postgres, Kubernetes, and Amazon providers.

steps.title: Start Airflow
steps.text: The `standalone` command starts the scheduler and the web server with a local SQLite database. This repo is the DAGs folder. Use the `apache/airflow:2.9.3` image: in the 2.10.5 image, 18 DAGs fail to import, because its Postgres provider no longer has `airflow.providers.postgres.operators`.

steps.title: Open the web UI
steps.text: Wait about one minute, then open http://localhost:8080 and log in as `admin`. Airflow writes the generated login for `admin` to a file in the container. This command shows it.

steps.title: Check the DAGs
steps.text: At this commit, 25 DAGs load and 3 files fail to import. `migrate_captures_dag.py` and `migrate_stakeholders_dag.py` need Airflow variables from the Greenstand environment (for example, `DATABASE_LOGIN`). `species_id_dag.py` has a syntax error.
code: docker exec treetracker-airflow airflow dags list-import-errors

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.text: Only `lib/utils_test.py` runs without Greenstand services. The other tests in `lib/` need a Greenstand database (`DB_URL`), AWS keys, or calls to live URLs.
